q: Which grid emission factor does a wind or solar project in India use for emission reductions?
title: Grid factor for Indian wind and solar projects
short: A large project under ACM0002 must use the combined margin. For wind and solar, CEA's own worked example weights the operating margin 75% and build margin 25%: 0.75 x 0.962 + 0.25 x 0.446 gives 0.833 t CO2 per MWh, using a three-year operating margin.
audience: Developers of grid-connected wind and solar projects preparing carbon credit baselines

ol: Project: 100 MW wind farm, 312,500 MWh a year to the grid.
Operating margin fixed ex ante as the generation-weighted average of FY 2023-24 to FY 2025-26: 0.962.
Combined margin with 75:25 weights for intermittent sources: 0.833.
Projected reductions: 312,500 x 0.833 = 260,312.5 t CO2 a year.

p: A project under 15 MW using AMS-I.D may choose the weighted average instead. CEA's example for a 5 MW hydro station uses 0.675 for FY 2025-26, giving 11,812.5 t CO2 a year on 17,500 MWh.
Methodology versions and weights change. Confirm the rules of the programme you register under, whether CCTS, Verra or Gold Standard, before fixing a factor in the project design document.

senseible: Senseible keeps dated, site-level records from invoices and meter documents, useful as monitoring evidence. It does not register projects or issue carbon credits.
